title: Stable and quantitative small-scale laboratory propagation of Cryptocaryon irritans
author: Watanabe, How, et al.

steps.title: Obtain or generate theronts
steps.instruction: Collect theronts from a seawater‑adapted black‑molly culture kept in a seawater aquarium with a biological filter (Yoshinaga et al., 1994). If no culture exists, obtain infected ornamental or food fish, keep them overnight in a filtered‑seawater aquarium to let protomonts detach, wash protomonts with filter‑sterilized seawater containing 500 IU/mL penicillin G K and 500 µg/mL streptomycin sulfate, and incubate at 25 °C in the same antibiotic‑supplemented seawater until theronts appear (Yoshinaga et al., 1994).

substeps.instruction: Collect theronts from an existing C. irritans culture.

If needed, generate theronts: obtain infected fish → overnight incubation in filtered seawater → wash protomonts with seawater + antibiotics (500 IU/mL penicillin G K, 500 µg/mL streptomycin) → incubate at 25 °C to obtain theronts.

steps.title: Challenge naïve fish with theronts
steps.instruction: Place five naïve black mollies (3–4 cm, 0.7–1.5 g) together with 5 000 theronts (1 000 theronts per fish) in 1.5 L of filtered seawater inside a 2 L plastic aquarium, keep at 25 °C, in the dark, inside an incubator for 6 h. Maintain all fish‑rearing and tomont‑incubation steps at 25 °C.

steps.title: Transfer fish to fresh seawater
steps.instruction: After the 6‑h challenge, move the fish to a new 2 L plastic aquarium containing 1.5 L of fresh filtered seawater; keep the aquarium in the dark with gentle aeration.

steps.title: Move fish to net basket
steps.instruction: Forty‑eight hours after the challenge, when trophonts appear as pin‑head white spots on skin and fins, transfer the fish into a plastic net basket placed in 1.0 L of filtered seawater inside a 1.5 L plastic aquarium; keep the setup in the dark inside the incubator.

steps.title: Allow protomont detachment
steps.instruction: Leave the fish and basket in the aquarium for the next 24 h so that protomonts detach from the fish, settle, and encyst as tomonts on the aquarium bottom; then remove the fish and basket.

steps.title: Rinse and incubate tomonts
steps.instruction: Rinse the aquarium bottom three times with filter‑sterilized seawater containing 500 IU/mL penicillin G K and 500 µg/mL streptomycin sulfate, leaving 50 mL of this antibiotic‑supplemented seawater in the tank. Incubate the tank with a 12 h light / 12 h dark photoperiod (6:00–18:00 light, 18:00–6:00 dark). Replace the seawater with fresh filtered seawater daily.

substeps.instruction: Rinse bottom three times with seawater + antibiotics (500 IU/mL penicillin G K, 500 µg/mL streptomycin).
Leave 50 mL of the antibiotic seawater in the tank.
Incubate with 12 h light/12 h dark (6:00–18:00 light).
Replace seawater with fresh filtered seawater each day.

steps.title: Collect and quantify theronts
steps.instruction: Five to seven days after step 6, when tomonts release theronts (mainly 6–3 h before the end of the dark period), collect the theront suspension from the aquarium. Determine theront concentration by counting cells in five 50 µL aliquots placed in 96‑well plates and examined under an inverted microscope. Use the counted theronts for the next infection or experiments.

steps.title: Repeat propagation cycle
steps.instruction: For the next round of infection, return to step 2 and repeat steps 2 through 7.
